scope: Theorem 12.4 (Signed-palette transfer) of the manuscript “From partial permutation information to Fourier bounds” (preprints/From-partial-permutation-information-to-Fourier-bounds-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 88926b5e48099ed8), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 41-42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n tend to infinity through even integers. For each n, partition [n] = A ⊔ B into equal halves and let µ be a probability on Sn. Suppose that εn → 0 and that, for every palette on either half, every placement of its classes, its subgroup H, and every x ∈ Sn, µ(xH) ≤ [Sn : H]−1 exp{vH(p) + εn}. (12.8) Here δ and v satisfy (12.7). For all sufficiently large n, uniformly over λ / ∈ {(n), (1n)}, ∥b µ(λ)∥2 HS ≤ D −1/3 λ , (12.9) ∥b µ(λ)∥op ≤ D −1/6 λ . (12.10) 41 If in addition |b µ(sgn)| = o(1), then ∥µ∗4 −USn ∥TV = o(1), and consequently ∥µ∗30 −USn ∥TV = o(1) as well. Both conclusions also hold with µ replaced in every factor by a probability µ0 satisfying ∥µ0 − µ∥TV = o(1).
